s5.title: Request for Pit Scouting data from CMP please (post 5, Roebling data)

s6.title: The search after good shooting robots (post 15)

demand.text: In qualification matches the team said it had to climb for the ranking point, since some partners could not reach the traversal or high rung. In playoffs with two partners able to traverse, a team member would stay out and shoot for more points.

auto.text: A post says 176 made 49 of 50 autonomous shots in qualification matches at the championship.

cycle.text: The intake lifts cargo over the bumper and belts push it to the middle of the tunnel. Two color sensors fill the LED strips when two balls are in. In soft lock the turret follows the hub wherever it is; the robot stops briefly to focus and shoots.

endgame.text: The operator presses one button. The climber takes the mid bar, skipping the low one, then repeats its move to the high bar and the traversal.

fallback.text: If soft lock holds a different target, the robot goes to hard lock and back to soft lock before shooting; this happened in the match before the interview. Wrong-color cargo is ejected by an operator button.

changed.text: The climber was designed a couple of times: another design would have been a little faster, but the team prototyped it and could not get it to work. Metal plates were added to the intake's stressed points, and flaps where balls pinched. A team member says the turret or shooter had to be redesigned because it was too heavy with the climber on.

outcome.text: 65-6-0 in official play; ranked 18 of the pooled top 20 (OPR 56.94, Roebling).

facts.text: Listed as tank drive in a post of Roebling pit scouting data

solves.text: Pick up cargo and survive hits while the intake is out

facts.text: Compliant, so it moves around when the robot is hit
The pneumatic cylinders are retracted while the intake is out and extend to raise it, so they do not get bent
Compression had to be found by experiment so the ball would rise over the bumper
Screws keep the bearings in the polycarbonate, and metal plates back the points most likely to be hit
Flaps keep balls from getting stuck where they pinched

solves.text: Keep a ball from getting stuck on the way into the tunnel

facts.text: Two NEOs run the belts, which push the ball toward the middle
Inner wheels and sticky tape help hold the balls in place

solves.text: Tell the drivers from afar how many balls are in and what mode the robot is in

facts.text: Color sensors
With one ball one strip lights; with two the whole strip lights
The LEDs change color for climb mode
Programmed in Java, with a Raspberry Pi on the robot

solves.text: Aim well at the hub from wherever the robot is on the field

facts.text: Base 3D printed in sections
Soft lock follows a rough estimate of the hub; hard lock locks onto the target and shoots
Soft lock became precise enough that the robot only stops for a little to focus before shooting
Described as able to spin 360 degrees, stopping because of the hose
Roebling pit scouting data in a post also lists a turret

solves.text: Put spin on the ball so it is less likely to bounce out of the hub

facts.text: Two wheel sizes, about 2 in and about 4 in
One set spins a little faster, and the wheels give the ball spin
A team member thinks the ball leaves with a little top spin
One set of wheels is harder than most teams use but expand a little when shooting; several durometers were tried
Machined in the team's shop

solves.text: Climb from the mid bar to the traversal with one operator button

facts.text: The elevator hooks the mid bar and pulls down until the bar latches onto fixed hooks
Pneumatics then pivot the elevator out, about
It then goes under the next bar, hits it and pulls up, which releases the hooks from the bar below and brings them to the next one
Skips the low bar to be faster
Almost fully automated

decisions.choice: Keep the intake cylinders retracted while the intake is out
decisions.because: the cylinders are protected and do not get bent, an issue the team had in the past
the other design could not be made to work in prototyping
decisions.instead_of: another climber design that would be a little faster

decisions.choice: Give the ball some spin with one set of wheels running faster
decisions.because: it has less of a chance of bouncing out of the hub
